{{nihongo|'''Ōgata Shrine'''|大形神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

'''Oogata Shrine''' (おおがたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Kawawatari Honmachi, {{ill|Higashi-ku, Niigata|Q711707|qid=Q711707|lt=Higashi Ward}}, {{ill|Niigata (city)|Q179691|qid=Q179691}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|Q132705|qid=Q132705}}.

=== Overview ===
The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-kami}}.
The shrine stands in a low-lying, marshy area near the {{ill|River mouth|Q1233637|qid=Q1233637}} of the {{ill|Shinano River|Q734455|qid=Q734455}} and {{ill|Agano River|Q390458|qid=Q390458}} on the {{ill|Echigo Plain|Q1045299|qid=Q1045299}}. Because it sits on a raised section corresponding to the hills of the {{ill|Niigata Sand Dunes|Q17209735|qid=Q17209735}}, it has long been a site where settlements formed.
In addition to the {{ill|Honden|Q2044994|qid=Q2044994}} and {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}}, the {{ill|keidai|Q11429002|qid=Q11429002}} include a {{ill|Kagura-den|Q94498|qid=Q94498}} and several {{ill|Massha|Q135009906|qid=Q135009906}}: Shinmei Shrine, Inari Shrine, and Furumine Shrine. About 1 km to the northwest, on the shore of the west pond of Junsai Pond, stands Kamimichi Shrine, regarded as an auxiliary shrine outside the grounds.
The haiden is an {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=irimoya-style}} structure with a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=chidori hafu}} gable.
In the front garden stands a {{ill|Double-flowered|Q63825|qid=Q63825}} {{ill|Kizakura|Q11677776|qid=Q11677776}}, making the shrine a noted scenic spot.

=== History ===
The founding of the shrine is said to date to the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, during the Daidō era ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}}–{{ill|810|Q23819|qid=Q23819}}). In the shrine register (Shinmyōchō) of the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}, compiled in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Enchō 5}} (927), it is listed as Oogata Shrine of Numatare District, one of the five shrines of that district. The “{{ill|jinjameisaichou|Q11590704|qid=Q11590704}}” compiled in {{ill|1884|Q7819|qid=Q7819}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Meiji 17}}) records it as Hakusan Shrine enshrining Kikurihime-no-Mikoto, though when this change occurred is unknown. Plaques and sacred mirrors from about 100 years ago bear the name Oogata Shrine. === Festivals and Events ===
=== {{ill|Shinto ritual|Q11588671|qid=Q11588671}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Festivals}} ===
* {{ill|Sai-no-Kami|Q115978710|qid=Q115978710}} ritual – around {{ill|January 15|Q2260|qid=Q2260}} ({{ill|koshōgatsu|Q137803901|qid=Q137803901}})
* Spring Festival – {{ill|April 17|Q2520|qid=Q2520}}
* Autumn Festival – first Friday and Saturday of September
* Oogata Shrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Daidai Kagura}}
** A {{ill|Shinto ritual|Q11588671|qid=Q11588671}} handed down for about 200 years by the Terayama family, who serve as {{ill|Kannushi (disambiguation)|Q15888735|qid=Q15888735}}. During the autumn festival, the doors of the main hall are opened and eleven dances of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Izumo style}} are performed and dedicated. Designated as a municipal cultural heritage.

=== Outside the Grounds ===
* Kamimichi Shrine (かみみちじんじゃ)
** Deity: Ryūrei-shin
** {{ill|June 18|Q2670|qid=Q2670}}
** Located in Matsuzono 2-chōme, Higashi Ward, Niigata City, on the south side of the west pond of Junsai Pond; established on {{ill|July 30|Q2716|qid=Q2716}}, {{ill|Template: Location map Pakistan|Q12359|qid=Q12359}} (Shōwa 25). It has a main hall, haiden, and a stone statue of Kannon Bosatsu.

=== Oogata Shrine and the District Name ===
In August {{ill|1901|Q2035|qid=Q2035}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 34), the three villages of Shin-Matsushima, Sanga, and Nihonoka in Niigata Prefecture merged and took the name {{ill|Ōgata|Q11435417|qid=Q11435417|lt=Oogata Village}} from this shrine. The village was incorporated into Niigata City on June 1, {{ill|1943|Q18623|qid=Q18623}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}} 18), and is now part of Higashi Ward, Niigata City; however, the shrine itself is not located within the present Oogata district but in the {{ill|Kawawatari|Q17128357|qid=Q17128357}} district.
